careers at Boroondara Become a school crossing supervisor Become a school crossing supervisor Listen Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Print Content components School crossing supervisors have a much-valued role in Boroondara. On an average school day in Boroondara, they help 9,266 pedestrians to cross the street while 74,426 motor vehicles use our roads during school crossing times. We are always looking for school crossing supervisors. If you are friendly, reliable and flexible, this role is for you. What does a school crossing supervisor do? This paid position gives you the opportunity to get involved in your community and improve road safety for children, people with a disability and the general public who use our 114 school crossings. School crossing supervisors: • work part-time Monday to Friday, from 8 am to 9 am and from 3 pm to 4 pm, during the school term • play an important role in educating children with ‘Stop, Look and Listen’ instructions • are responsible for reporting any road hazards or potential risks • help to encourage active and independent travel. About you We are looking for people aged 18 and older who: • can attend shifts at short notice • have their own reliable transport • are able to work across several locations • can complete the pre-employment medical and police checks. You will have access to a full training program before starting your role. Download the position description School Crossing Supervisor PD 144.04 KB [PDF] 23 November 2022 How to apply Learn more about this rewarding role by reading the position description above. Submit an online application through our Careers website . Attend an interview – meet with one of our Council Officers at Council, located at 8 Inglesby Road in Camberwell. Provide us with relevant employment documents – including your Working With Children Check, Police Check and evidence of your COVID-19 vaccination status. Complete a medical assessment. Apply to become a School Crossings Supervisor We are always recruiting new school crossing supervisors to help people to cross our roads safely at peak school times. A little bit about the role The Information Management and Archives Officer coordinates and manages Council’s archives, supporting the effective lifecycle management of physical and electronic records. This role is critical to ensuring that Council records are managed, stored and disposed of in accordance with statutory, organisational and operational requirements. The Information Management Archives Officer contributes to high-quality records and information management services through the classification, capture and distribution of incoming information; secure mail room and file delivery services; and support for Information Management projects, audits and continuous improvement initiatives. The role is expected to Maintaining confidentiality and provide responsive support to internal stakeholders is a key expectation for this position. Key responsibilities include: Coordinate and manage Council’s archival services, including the appraisal, classification, storage, retrieval and disposal of physical and electronic records. Ensure records are managed in accordance with legislative, statutory, organisational and operational requirements, including PROV standards. Maintain accurate and secure records management tools, registers and catalogues to support compliance and searchability. Respond to requests for archived records, including retrieval, distribution and return. The provision of timely information management advice, assistance and support to internal stakeholders. Identify and escalate complex, high-risk or non-routine records management matters. Liaise with external service providers, including archive storage providers. Support mail, courier and information processing services, including the capture, registration and distribution of incoming and outgoing information. Support information management projects, audits, digitisation, quality assurance and continuous improvement initiatives. Maintain confidentiality and contribute to accurate, efficient and customer-focused information management services. A little bit about you You will have a relevant qualification in records management or a related discipline, or significant demonstrated experience in records, archives or information management. You will understand the legislative and regulatory requirements for public records management, ideally within a local government environment. You will have relevant experience in the use of electronic document and records management systems, with a strong understanding of classification structure and information organisation. You will bring strong attention to detail, sound judgement, problem-solving ability and the capacity to manage priorities, plan your own work to meet deadlines with minimal supervision. A current Victorian Driver Licence is required. Want to know more You can connect further and gain a better insight into this opportunity by reviewing the Position Description Employment requirements Applicants must have the right to work in Australia Preferred applicants will be required to undergo a National Police Record Check How to apply If you are an organised and detail-focused professional with experience in records, archives or information management, and you enjoy supporting others to manage information accurately and securely, we’d love to hear from you. Skip to Main Content Career Opportunities: Tree Crew Supervisor (15245) Requisition ID 15245 - Posted - Job Function (1) - Tenure Status (1) - Employment Status (1)  Job Description Print Preview Apply Save Job Email Job to Friend Return to List Full time, permanent position with our Tree Team, located in Kew Lead a skilled team, build capability and teamwork and make a lasting impact through people leadership $89,002 - $102,806 plus super, allowances and overtime available 9 day fortnight including a tool of trade vehicle The Role We are seeking an experienced and motivated leader to join our Open Space and Trees team as Tree Crew Supervisor. You will lead a team of arborists and apprentices responsible for delivering Council’s 24/7 reactive tree maintenance services. This hands-on leadership role combines people management with operational oversight. You will develop team capability, support employee growth, drive performance and wellbeing, and create an environment where people are empowered to do their best work. Key Responsibilities You will lead, coach and develop a team of arborists and apprentices, building a culture of accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement. You will support employee development through regular feedback, mentoring and performance conversations while promoting safety, wellbeing and exceptional customer service. You will oversee daily operations, coordinate resources and prioritise works to ensure service delivery objectives are achieved. You will also build strong relationships across Council, contractors and the community to support positive outcomes and service excellence. About You You have proven experience leading operational teams, building capability, managing performance and fostering positive workplace cultures. You are confident providing direction, building trust and empowering employees to achieve their best. With strong communication and stakeholder management skills, you can balance operational demands with a genuine commitment to people, safety and continuous improvement. You have strong communication and interpersonal skills, sound judgement and the ability to balance operational priorities with people-focused leadership. Your ability to motivate teams, foster collaboration and maintain positive stakeholder relationships will be critical to your success in this role. For more information about the role, please refer to the position description. Join the City of Boroondara At the City of Boroondara, we are proud to serve a vibrant, diverse and engaged community. Guided by our values and commitment to delivering exceptional customer experience, we work together to build a sustainable and inclusive city. Our people are passionate about what they do, united by a shared purpose and driven to continuously explore better ways of working. How to apply Please submit your application online via the ‘Apply Now’ button by 11.59pm, Wednesday 7 October 2026 . All applications must be made via the online portal; no applications direct to the hiring manager or from recruitment agencies will be considered. Skip to Main Content Career Opportunities: Test Analyst (15243) Requisition ID 15243 - Posted - Job Function (1) - Tenure Status (1) - Employment Status (1)  Job Description Print Preview Apply Save Job Email Job to Friend Return to List Great opportunity to be part of an exciting transformation program Camberwell location, full time limited tenure position until 31 August 2027 $104,790- $114,015 salary per annum (Plus super and RDO) Great opportunity to contribute to ensuring quality and testing for a high-profile transformation program that will shape how Council delivers services to the community. A little bit about the role Council’s Property, Planning and Permits (PPP) program is modernising how Council delivers services to the community. The PPP program is implementing Datascape and MyDatascape across property, planning, building and regulatory services, supported by significant business-process change, integrations, data migration and financial and regulatory controls. Council requires credible, independent evidence that the new capability is fit for purpose, operationally ready and sustainable through future SaaS releases. The Test Analyst provides hands-on functional testing across the PPP project’s customer, staff and operational processes. The role works with subject matter experts, business analysts, process owners, suppliers and users to translate requirements, process designs, business rules, user journeys and acceptance criteria into realistic scenarios, test cases, exploratory testing, walkthroughs and UAT support. The role works with employees at all levels across Council and with Senior Test Lead, will work with SaaS vendor functional specialists, migration and integration suppliers testing-tool vendors and specialist assurance providers. Key responsibilities include: Work with SMEs, business analysts and process owners to define realistic test scenarios, expected outcomes, test data and acceptance evidence. Apply risk-based testing priorities across customer, operational, financial, regulatory and service-delivery impacts. Prepare functional testing materials, including test scenarios, test cases, exploratory testing charters, walkthrough packs and evidence expectations. Coordinate testing inputs such as business data, environments, user roles, preconditions and SME participation. Support UAT activities, including business user support, defect triage, retesting and evidence review. Execute functional and end-to-end testing across process flows, user journeys, roles, regression, cutover rehearsal and production verification. Validate key business processes, including approvals, notifications, payments, refunds, hand-offs, exceptions, business rules and data outcomes. Capture test evidence and manage defects by raising clear defects, retesting fixes, assessing regression impacts and escalating unresolved risks. Support informed acceptance decisions by providing credible evidence on readiness, residual risks and functional quality. A little bit about you You will be a practical, detail-oriented Test Analyst who enjoys working closely with business users, SMEs, analysts, suppliers and technical teams to test complex systems, this role will suit you. You will bring demonstrated hands-on experience designing and executing functional, process-flow, user-journey and end-to-end testing across integrated SaaS, ERP or enterprise environments. You will be confident translating requirements, business processes and acceptance criteria into realistic test scenarios, clear expected results and credible evidence. You will apply a risk-based mindset to testing, focusing on customer, operational, financial, regulatory and service-delivery impacts. You are organised, analytical and collaborative, with strong communication skills and the ability to document test cases, defects, evidence and residual risks clearly for both technical and non-technical audiences. You will be confident supporting UAT, walkthroughs, defect triage and retesting, and have the ability to support business stakeholders make informed acceptance decisions. You will have strong knowledge of system, functional, end-to-end, regression testing, UAT support, testing, cutover rehearsal, and production-verification testing across customer, staff and operational processes. ISTQB Foundation or equivalent professional certification will be highly regarded. We are interested to hear about your experience as relevant to this position, there are some questions you will be asked to answer as part of your application for this position. All applications must be made via the online portal by Wednesday 7 October 2026 at 11.59pm . No applications direct to the hiring manager or from recruitment agencies will be considered. Skip to Main Content Career Opportunities: Technical Test Analyst (15244) Requisition ID 15244 - Posted - Job Function (1) - Tenure Status (1) - Employment Status (1)  Job Description Print Preview Apply Save Job Email Job to Friend Return to List Great opportunity to be part of an exciting transformation program Camberwell location, full time limited tenure position until 31 August 2027 $104,790- $114,015 salary per annum (Plus super and RDO) Great opportunity to contribute to ensuring quality and testing for a high-profile transformation program that will shape how Council delivers services to the community. A little bit about the role Council’s Property, Planning and Permits (PPP) program is modernising how Council delivers services to the community. The PPP program is implementing Datascape and MyDatascape across property, planning, building and regulatory services, supported by significant business-process change, integrations, data migration and financial and regulatory controls. Council requires credible, independent evidence that the new capability is fit for purpose, operationally ready and sustainable through future SaaS releases. The Technical Test Analyst provides hands-on technical testing across Datascape, MyDatascape, APIs, integrations, data migration and connected Council systems. The role implements and maintains the agreed test-automation framework and approved test tooling; develops reliable UI, API, integration, data-validation and migration-reconciliation automation; and performs manual technical testing where automation is not appropriate. The role works with employees at all levels across Council and with Senior Test Lead, will work with SaaS vendor functional specialists, migration and integration suppliers testing-tool vendors and specialist assurance providers. Key responsibilities include: Identify and prioritise technical quality risks by reviewing requirements, supplier specifications, APIs, interfaces, migration rules and acceptance criteria. Translate high-risk business processes into clear, testable technical scenarios in collaboration with functional testers, SMEs and technical teams. Define testability needs, including accessible APIs, stable UI selectors, logging, traceability, controlled test data, test accounts and repeatable environments. Establish, maintain and improve the approved automation framework, reusable components, tools, repositories, dashboards and evidence structures. Build and maintain reliable automated testing across UI, API, integration, data validation, migration reconciliation, smoke and regression coverage. Design and execute API, integration, migration, reconciliation, regression, cutover and production-safe verification testing across connected systems. Validate data flows, cross-system transactions, hand-offs, referential integrity, failure scenarios, retries, outages and recovery behaviour. Provide credible technical evidence, analyse defects, support UAT and end-to-end testing, retest fixes and escalate unresolved quality risks. A little bit about you You will be a hands-on technical test analyst with experience working on complex SaaS, ERP or enterprise system implementations. You will bring strong practical capability in API testing, integration validation, data migration, SQL or data interrogation, automation design and technical defect diagnosis. You are confident building and maintaining reliable automated tests using tools such as Playwright or equivalent, and understand how to manage testware through source control, reusable components, controlled configuration and secure test-data practices. You will have a risk-based approach to testing, balancing coverage, reliability, execution time and maintenance effort. You will be able to critically assess supplier evidence, identify technical quality risks and support robust regression, recovery, cutover and production-verification testing. You will have well developed analytical and communication skills and the ability to work constructively with functional testers, business SMEs, technical teams and suppliers. ISTQB Certified Tester Foundation level qualification and Advanced Level Test Automation Engineering certification would be desirable. A little bit about the role City of Boroondara is a leader in the Local Government sector and one of the nation’s most liveable municipal councils. The Team Leader Compliance plays a key role in the leadership of the Civic Services Department, which deliver multiple regulatory services to protect the health, safety, amenity and assets of the city. Skip to Main Content Career Opportunities: Local Laws Officer (15251) Requisition ID 15251 - Posted - Job Function (1) - Tenure Status (1) - Employment Status (1)  Job Description Print Preview Apply Save Job Email Job to Friend Return to List Local Laws Officer Join a dynamic, investigations team that supports each other to succeed Deliver meaningful outcomes to the community in safety and amenity $93,845 -101,184 per annum (plus super) Tool of trade vehicle provided (non-hybrid position) Join us in building a professional investigations team and help deliver a responsive, community-focused Local Laws service. In this role, you will contribute to a safe, liveable and well-maintained municipality while providing high-quality regulatory service to residents and stakeholders. About the role At City of Boroondara, our Local Laws directly contributes to our purpose of protecting the health, safety, amenity and assets of the municipality. Based within the large and busy department of Civic Services, the team works as part of five field-based teams and many others within the Urban Living Directorate. You will respond to reported breaches of the Amenity Local Law and the Environment Protection Act, using education, investigation and enforcement to achieve compliance. The role involves managing a varied caseload, gathering evidence, preparing clear records and working within established procedures to resolve matters fairly and effectively. The position includes investigating issues such as illegally dumped rubbish under the EPA, unsightly properties, overhanging vegetation, illegally advertising and the occupation of Council land, while providing courteous and timely service to community members. From time to time, you will also support the Animal Management team with park patrols, and work with external stakeholders including Victoria Police, the Magistrates’ Court and Council prosecutors. Hours are allocated over a 16-week roster (42-hours per week) and rotating weekend work is required every 4 weeks with penalty rates that convert into an annualised salary. A fully maintained vehicle is provided as a ‘tool of trade’ to perform necessary duties and commute to and from work. This is a non-hybrid role as our ‘office’ is in the community, every day and our success comes from working together with other officers, as a team! About you We are looking for someone who brings sound judgement, a strong customer focus and a collaborative approach. You will be supported to build your knowledge and succeed in the role. You will have experience delivering customer service in a complex regulatory environment or another fast-paced setting, with the ability to communicate clearly, build rapport and respond professionally in a range of situations under pressure. Experience in areas such as retail, hospitality, community services or other enforcement role can provide a strong foundation for success in this role. You will be able to investigate issues methodically, collect information accurately and prepare clear notes and reports. Knowledge of compliance, local laws or related legislation will be well regarded, as will the ability to interpret policy and apply it in practical situations. If you are still developing in these areas, a willingness to learn will be equally valued. Full-time permanent position $104,790- $114, 015 Band 6 plus Superannuation plus RDO At the City of Boroondara, we're committed to creating a healthy, connected and sustainable community. We're seeking an experienced and motivated Community Wellbeing Administration Lead to oversee the administration of our highly regarded Immunisation Service and support the delivery of essential public health programs to our community. This is an exciting opportunity for a collaborative leader who enjoys improving systems, supporting people and ensuring services run efficiently and effectively. About the Role Reporting to the Community Wellbeing Senior Coordinator, you will lead a small administration team responsible for supporting Council's Immunisation Service. You'll play a key role in coordinating vaccination programs, managing service administration, overseeing systems and processes, and ensuring compliance with relevant legislative and public health requirements. Working closely with nurses, Maternal and Child Health teams, schools, community groups and government agencies, you'll help deliver high-quality services that support the health and wellbeing of Boroondara residents. Key responsibilities include: Leading the day-to-day administration of Council's Immunisation Service. Coordinating school, community, workplace and staff vaccination programs. Overseeing rostering, service systems, reporting and data quality. Managing contracts, procurement processes and budget monitoring. Supporting continuous improvement initiatives and service innovation. Leading and developing a high-performing administration team. Building strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders. Contributing to public health emergency preparedness and response activities. About You You are an organised and proactive people leader with strong administrative and operational management skills. The Boroondara Volunteer Resource Centre (BVRC) is seeking an enthusiastic and experienced Diversity & Inclusion Project Officer (Volunteering) to lead an exciting Volunteer Management Activity (VMA) project focused on reducing barriers to volunteering and helping community organisations create more inclusive volunteer programs. This role provides a unique opportunity to influence the future of volunteering by supporting organisations to engage and retain volunteers from diverse backgrounds while strengthening community connections and social inclusion. About the Role Reporting to the Volunteer Support and Development Lead, you will coordinate initiatives that increase participation in volunteering among: Young people aged 12 to 18 People with disability and/or mental health challenges Vulnerable women People experiencing unemployment First Nations peoples Newly arrived migrants Working within the BVRC, you will collaborate with volunteer-involving organisations, community groups, Council staff and sector partners to deliver projects, training, events and resources that support inclusive volunteering practices. What You'll Be Doing Deliver a flagship diversity and inclusion volunteering event featuring expert speakers and lived-experience perspectives. Recruit, train and support Volunteer Ambassadors who promote volunteering within the community. Design and facilitate workshops, learning programs and capacity-building initiatives for volunteer-involving organisations. Develop practical resources, communications and promotional materials that encourage inclusive volunteer engagement. Build strong relationships with community organisations, First Nations groups, multicultural organisations, faith-based groups and sector networks. Conduct outreach activities at community events, neighbourhood houses, schools, libraries and other community settings. We are seeking skilled and experienced professional care workers who love supporting people to live independently in the community. We currently provide services in Mount Alexander Shire and Central Goldfields Shire. This is your opportunity to bring your passion and skills to be part of a professional and dedicated team providing high quality in-home support to frail older people and people with disabilities in our community. The role provides tailored services to help clients live healthy, independent and active lives through assistance with daily tasks and activities. Direct Care Worker Traineeship Opportunities: If you don’t already have a certificate III in Individual Support, you can also apply here for a Trainee Direct Care Worker position, to earn and learn on the job. Minimum Qualifications and Experience You must have, or be willing to obtain: Current Police Check Current Working with Children Check Triple vaccinated for COVID (2 doses plus a booster). Current Drivers license and roadworthy, registered and comprehensively insured vehicle for work travel Applicants must be able to work weekends. First Aid and CPR certificate will be gained though training and applied to the role as required If you have any queries or would like to discuss the role, the key contacts are: Sarah Newstead In Home Support Coordinator – East (03) 5471 1845 Talia Jenkin In Home Support Coordinator – West (03) 5471 1728 To apply for a Direct Care Worker or Direct Care Worker Trainee position, please provide a cover letter (no more than 2 pages) outlining why you are interested and the best candidate for this role, and your current resume. Additional information Mount Alexander Shire Council is committed to providing a safe, inclusive, and respectful workplace. We are an equal opportunity employer and are committed to child safety with zero tolerance for child abuse. We value a diverse workforce and encourage applicants from all cultures, sexual orientations, gender identities and backgrounds. Applicants can expect that the recruitment process will include interviewing, reference checks and criminal history checks. Some positions will also be required to provide a Working with Children Check, and medical assessments including drug and alcohol testing may be undertaken. For more information on the recruitment process, please download the Candidate information document from our website.
